features.title: Router External Template Loading (templateUrl)
features.description: Added support for loading view templates from external HTML files, dramatically improving code organisation and maintainability for SPA applications
features.details:
Views can now load HTML templates from separate files:

Instead of embedding large HTML strings in JavaScript, use templateUrl to reference external .html files. This provides proper syntax highlighting, cleaner code organisation, and better separation of concerns.

Key features:

  • Template caching — Templates are fetched once and cached for the session, improving performance on repeat navigation
  • Parallel partial loading — Reusable template sections (partials) are loaded concurrently with the main template
  • Mustache syntax support — Use {{variable}}, {{#if}}, {{#each}}, and {{> partial}} in external templates
  • Organised file structure — Recommended layout with js/views/templates/ directories

Benefits: Views with 400+ lines of inline HTML reduced to ~50 lines of clean JavaScript. HTML files get proper editor support, and logic stays separate from presentation.

features.title: Kickstart Template Augmented Development
features.description: Enhanced the SPA kickstart template with built-in convention enforcement for AI-assisted development (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.)
features.details:
New projects now include:

  • CLAUDE.md — Consumer-focused convention enforcement with quick reference tables for Domma APIs
  • Memory file — Persistent reminders of core patterns and common mistakes
  • Updated settings — templateUrl patterns and reminders built into the project configuration

Developers using AI assistants get immediate guidance on Domma conventions, preventing common mistakes like using fetch() instead of H.get() or localStorage instead of S.set().

enhancements.title: Router Showcase Comprehensive Tutorial
enhancements.description: Added extensive Template Files tutorial section to router showcase with 6 sub-sections covering all aspects of external template usage
enhancements.details:
New tutorial sections cover:

  • Problem/solution comparison (before/after examples)
  • Basic templateUrl usage with clear examples
  • Template variables and Mustache syntax
  • Partials for reusable template sections
  • Template caching behaviour and performance
  • Recommended file organisation patterns

The router is now discoverable from the showcase hub, and best practices have been updated to explicitly recommend templateUrl for views with more than a few lines of HTML.

enhancements.title: Enhanced Detail Formatting
enhancements.description: Improved release notes formatting with proper HTML structure for better readability
enhancements.details:
Release note details now use structured HTML with paragraphs, lists, and inline code formatting instead of plain text arrays.

This provides better visual hierarchy and makes complex feature descriptions easier to scan and understand.

bugFixes.title: Effects Motion Preference Override
bugFixes.description: Fixed critical issue where reveal() and ripple() effects were being disabled by CSS media queries even when JavaScript explicitly set respectMotionPreference: false
bugFixes.details:
Root cause: CSS @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) queries were applying globally, overriding JavaScript configuration.

Solution:

  • Added data-force-animation attribute to elements when motion preference should be ignored
  • Updated CSS media queries to exclude elements with this attribute
  • Fixed ripple effect to apply the attribute to dynamically created ripple elements

Impact: Showcase demo pages now work correctly regardless of user's system motion preferences, ensuring animations display when explicitly configured.

bugFixes.title: Showcase Effects Pages Cleanup
bugFixes.description: Cleaned up effects showcase pages by removing references to obsolete overrideMotionPreference variable
bugFixes.details:
Updated all showcase pages to use respectMotionPreference: false consistently.

Fixed 14 remaining references across 3 showcase files, ensuring consistent behaviour and removing deprecated API usage.
